newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end flat after see-saw session.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end flat after see-saw session.

text.p: Japanese stocks closed marginally lower on Tuesday after a volatile session in which the key market index nosedived more than 500 points but managed to claw back most of its losses.
Brokers said demand for blue-chip stocks fuelled the rebound from the early plunge.
The key Nikkei average of 225 leading shares closed 25.66 points or 0.14 percent lower at 18,093.13.

The index had earlier plunged more than 500 points to 17,545.52 after failing to sustain a robust rebound on Monday from a succession of slides on worries about the economy and the health of the banking industry.

But a late surge of interest in big-name shares such as Honda spared the market yet another loss, triggering a bounce in afternoon trade that briefly took the Nikkei into positive territory shortly before the close.

"Domestic investors, including pension funds and some foreign investors, started buying bellwether issues such as Honda Motor near the end of the session, helping erase the losses accumulated in the morning," said Akishige Ishikura, an analyst at Dai-ichi Securities.
